countsMean.frames: The sweep's own frame count, asserted by `check-evidence.mjs` against the frames on disk that fall outside any declared `supplementary` set - 752 at this head, and the assertion is the definition rather than a restatement of it: 882 `.webp` are committed and the 18 `supplementary` sets below account for 130 of them (one of those sets declares no frames), leaving 752. Both terms moved under this branch rather than in it: `main`'s #136 declared the sixteen `clear-search/` frames as a `supplementary` set, so at the rebase base the same three terms read 870 / 18 / 130 and the swept remainder was 740; this branch contributes the twelve frames the 2026-09-13 states needed - six `dracula` frames for panels that carried two themes, plus the two new states across three themes - and 882 - 130 = 752 is the arithmetic at this head. Re-derived for THIS head and stated once. Earlier revisions of this field appended a fresh derivation per merge and left the previous ones standing as though they still described the tree, so it accumulated half a dozen figures from superseded heads and, after the 0.19.5 rebase, a subtraction that no longer resolved - the sibling terms were updated and the remainder was not. Those figures are deleted rather than quoted here: a reader scanning this field for a number should not find a wrong one under any framing. A stale derivation is worse here than no derivation, because this field's entire justification is that a reader can re-compute it: one that does not resolve teaches them to stop checking. The three terms above are the whole arithmetic, they are read from the tree rather than transcribed (`find docs/evidence -name '*.webp' | wc -l`, and the summed `frames` of the sets below), and `check-evidence.mjs` fails when they disagree with it - which is what makes the sentence checkable rather than merely asserted. The update pair is a NARROWED refresh (see `partialCapture`) on top of the set `main` carried, so 752 is `main`'s 740 plus the 12 frames this branch adds: six `dracula` frames for update panels that carried two themes, and the two new stories (`install-in-flight`, `install-failed-cancelled-by-relaunch`) across the three refreshed themes. This branch carries no version bump of its own: `package.json` is `0.19.7` here and on `main`, the release that landed while this branch was in review.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head above - 110 entries, counted off the merged literal rather than summed from the two sides' fields. `main`'s own manifest at the rebase base carries 108, which the same assertion checks against that tree, and this branch adds the two states the 2026-09-13 incident needed and the app did not have - `common-updatenotification--install-in-flight` and `common-updatenotification--install-failed-cancelled-by-relaunch` - for 108 + 2 = 110. Counted, not added, because each side's field was written by a run taken before the other side landed - which is exactly why the merged figure is read off the literal. `check-evidence.mjs` counts the list and fails a mismatch (round 4, R3), so this field cannot silently lag its own source.

partialCapture.note: Round 2 of review, one narrowed pass: `--only=common-updatenotification-- --themes=localOperatorDark,localOperatorLight,dracula` re-rendered all 27 frames of this family at this head, 21 of which changed bytes, none added. The family is the honest scope rather than the two stories whose copy this round edits, because two of the findings land in SHARED code: `PanelDetails` now offers a break opportunity after each `/` in the value it renders, which reaches every panel carrying a details line, and the second `" - "` splice the review named is the cancelled-by-relaunch remedy. `install-blocked` and `update-available` came out byte-identical, which is why the diff is 21 files and not 27: the first details line is mostly prose that already breaks at its own spaces, and the second panel has no details line at all. What moved, then: the in-flight panel (the body names what staying open costs instead of restating the heading, the secondary's label carries the same cost, and the details path breaks at segment boundaries), `downloaded` (the pre-quit sentence promoted to `text-body` and split into three sentences), the cancelled-by-relaunch remedy (an em dash for the spliced clause), and the remaining details lines, whose breaks are now segment-aligned instead of mid-segment. The tool's guard REFUSED a normal run - a Local Operator backend owns 127.0.0.1:1111 on this machine, and it is the operator's live app instance, so it was neither stopped nor captured against - and `--allow-backend` is the tool's documented opt-in for a narrowed run whose surfaces never call out: every panel here renders from a fixture payload against a mocked `window.api`. The pass ran before the rebase onto `main`'s #136: the rebase was content-neutral for every frame in this directory - `git range-diff` differs only in the base-relative manifest context, the `+/--` line sets for `src/` and `scripts/` are byte-identical between the two heads, and the re-rendered `.webp` blobs hash the same - and what it moved is the stamps above, re-derived at this head.

The unit suite asserts the classes, the transitions and the reading rule (`scripts/picker-feedback.test.mjs`); only a frame of the running app shows the ground and the edge the row actually paints inside a dialog whose own ground is `elevated`, and what the user is left with when the answer arrives after the dialog is gone. The `before-*` halves carry the defect as a measurement: the active row's computed background is `rgb(40,35,24)`, identical to the dialog's, and `before-pointer-left-list` is byte-identical to `before-keyboard-highlight` (AE 0 of 4,813,440 px). The transcript note count is measured either side of the U2 case — 1 before the click, 2 after it, with the dialog closed 80 ms in — because the refusal sentence is identical for every refused pick and only a count can prove a second one was written. The U7 pair is measured rather than described: between the two frames AE is 85,307 px (1.77%) of 4,813,440, of which 13,230 px (2% fuzz) sit in one 952x64 band across the header sentence's own text line and 274 px are the clock.

supplementary.why: The claim is the ROW: one flex row whose line depends on the column's width, on the working-directory chip's real shrink behaviour and on the real button sizes (32px above a small window, 28px below). A story frame cannot express that - a hand-built row would certify a layout the product does not have (branding section 8, and the D2 finding in the design that produced this change) - so before/ and after/ are the same script, the same backend and the same sequence of measured composer-box widths, 78e694777 against this branch. The draft frames photograph the PANE and the strip is absent from them: the draft's readings need POST /v1/desktop/sessions/preview, which lives on the backend branch (draft_preview: 1) and is not on main, so the live end-to-end draft cell is pending that branch rather than implied here. The before set is localOperatorDark throughout: its light run came back dark and those frames were deleted rather than shipped mislabelled. Frame count repaired here from 23 to 34, and `surfaces` with it, on 2026-09-14: the set holds 34 `.webp` across 28 captured state directories, six of them in both themes, and #132 declared it before its last states landed. `check-evidence.mjs` checks each declaration against its own directory, so the under-declaration failed the gate on `main` as well. This branch already reconciles this file; the repair is two numbers, and if #132's author would rather own it, it is still two numbers.

supplementary.source: live renderer in the operator's real browser (Local Operator extension) at device-pixel-ratio 2, served by Vite over this repository's own renderer config with the preload bridge stubbed to a no-op, against an isolated local-operator backend on its own port and config dir - plus a second backend holding a 120-session store, which is what the clipped-answer state needs
supplementary.why: The claim is what a typed query does to the list the app fetched: which rows survive, which one is ranked first, which ones say the CONVERSATION is why they are there, and what the panel says when nothing matched. The sidebar has no Storybook story and a debounced backend round trip is not something a fixture produces, so the frames come from the running app against an isolated seeded store. RE-SHOT at the head named below: the set before it was taken at cf0db490e, before the marker row's slot classes changed, so it showed a layout the code could not produce (review round 6, R22/R26). Both ends of the sidebar clamp and both palettes are covered for the two row cases this set was for - a NESTED row at the default width (design round 5's D19) and a 64-character binding (review round 4's R21) - and the nested-280 pair was re-shot as a matched pair after design round 6 (D21) found its halves at different viewports. docs/evidence/chat-search/README.md carries the DOM boxes beside every row claim, which is where a clipping question is actually settled. TWO FRAMES IN IT ARE NOT PICTURES OF THIS TREE and the README says so at length: after-namesonly and after-searchfail are cf0db490e frames carrying a server is offline strip from a run where the backend had died, kept only for the notice copy they show, and replacing them is an open follow-up. The clipped-answer state is photographed at this head (after-clipped, the second store answering exactly its limit, badge 100+ and spoken as At least 100 matching); the light half of the long-binding pair is the one state still to be photographed, and the README names it as such. TWO CAPTURE SESSIONS, and the pixels do not move between them: bed8de048 re-shot the set, and the round-7 pass re-shot the nested-280 pair through a settle gate and added the clamp pair, the clipped answer and the counts' accessible names. the shipped sidebar did move under this set while it was being shot, and the frames say so: #136 put the clear control inside the search field (chat-sidebar.tsx to blob 8a0a6063) and #139 aligned the New chat row (to blob 308f13f8, which is what v0.20.1 and v0.21.0 ship), neither of them touching the row code this set photographs, which is why the ten re-shot frames were taken again at that base and the five that could not be are declared above. The only commits to the ROW since are the two accessibility-string fixes (c4b5f6b29, D23, and the D25 fix), which design round 7 measured against its own capture at MAE 0.000. (Round 10's M10: this clause used to claim origin/main had never touched the file and cite the 0.17.3 blob, which its own next sentence and README.md:20 already contradicted.) **THE SET SPANS TWO BASES AND THE README'S TABLE SAYS WHICH IS WHICH**: main moved 0.17.3 to 0.20.1 and landed #136 (a clear control inside the search field) and #139 (the New chat row alignment) in the same sidebar every frame shows. TEN after-* frames were re-shot at the 0.20.1 merge and show main's control - rest, retention both palettes, typo, no-match, nested-280 both, nested-240 both, longbinding-280 dark; FIVE were not, because the capture bridge dropped under this machine's load mid-session - unstarted, overlimit, clipped, longbinding-240, longbinding-280 light - and the before-* halves are still 0.17.3 for the same reason. What the split costs is bounded and checkable: the ROW readings at the merged head are identical number for number to the pre-merge ones (content 224.0/184.0, titles 120.0/103.0 and 80.0/63.3, statement slots 76.04 and 92.75 unclipped, the binding slot at 44.9% of its box), because the row code is this branch's and the merge did not touch it; what differs between the two bases is outside the rows this set is about: the FIELD above them (#136's clear control) and the `New chat` row's border, which #139 removed - design round 8 read both in the committed set, where `after-clipped` still shows the bordered row the re-shot frames have lost. No row this set photographs changed between the bases. Re-shooting the five remaining after-* frames and the before-* halves at 0.20.1 is the open follow-up. THE PER-FRAME READINGS ARE COMMITTED under readings/ beside the frames - each is what the harness POSTed from the page the frame names, the pair's taken at the shot - so every box in the README is checkable from the repository rather than from a gitignored directory.
